candidates.title: Genesee & Wyoming prepares to split into three rail holding companies
candidates.excerpt: Genesee & Wyoming Inc. is planning to separate into three rail holding companies, effective Jan. 1, 2027, a move that will position the regional entities for eventual sale. The companies will continue to be owned by G&W parent Brookfield and GIC. G&W operates more than 100 railroads. The new companies are: Atlantic & Great Lakes Transportation Inc., which will be made up of G&W operations in New England (including Berkshire & Eastern Railroad), New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. Atlantic & Great Lakes will be based in Rochester, N.Y., and led by Chief Executive Bill Keough, who has been with G&W for eight years and most recently served as regional senior vice president. Canyon & Cascade Transportation Inc., which will be comprised of G&W operations in Washington, Oregon, California, Arizona, and New Mexico. The project includes completing the rail station with six tracks and three center platforms; a station at Fourth and Townsend streets; and a 0.65-mile tunnel. candidates.title: Weekly U.S. rail traffic remains strong
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Continued strong intermodal volume helped weekly U.S. rail traffic remain well above 2025 levels for the week ending Nov. 7, 2026. According to statistics from the Association of American Railroads, traffic for the week was 526,283 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 6.6% over the same week a year ago. The overall figure included 227,914 carloads, an increase of 1.3%, and 298,369 intermodal units, a gain of 11%. For the year to date, U.S. railroads have handled 22,641,547 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.9% from the first 44 weeks of 2025. That includes 10,071,273 carloads, an increase of 2.7%, and 12,570,274 intermodal units, up 4.9%. North American figures for the week, from nine reporting U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, show total traffic of 721,559 carloads and intermodal units, up 6.7% from the corresponding week in 2025. candidates.title: GEODIS launches new rail freight connection between Italy and France
candidates.excerpt: GEODIS has launched a new rail freight service connecting Vicenza in northern Italy with Noisy-le-Sec, near Paris. The new route expands the company’s European intermodal network and provides another transport option for businesses in Italy’s Veneto region. The first train departed on 19 October 2026, marking the start of the service operated by Captrain and Hexafret. Both companies belong to Rail Logistics Europe, part of the SNCF Group alongside GEODIS. Initially, the service offers one departure per week in each direction. However, GEODIS plans to increase the frequency to two weekly departures per direction from January 2027. The connection is designed to transport several types of freight, including packaged liquid and powder goods. It also extends the company’s existing rail services in northern Italy, which already cover Lombardy, Piedmont and Emilia-Romagna through its Novara connection. The operation took place on 4 November at Xiamen Yuanhai Container Terminal, marking the first green methanol ship-to-ship bunkering operation in China’s Fujian province and expanding the port’s capabilities in alternative marine fuel supply. According to COSCO SHIPPING, the bunkering operation is estimated to deliver a reduction of more than 1,600 tonnes of carbon emissions compared with the use of conventional marine fuels. Intermodal volume rose 9.6% from a year earlier, with railroads handling an average of more than 298,000 containers and trailers per week — the highest weekly average for any month on record, according to the Association of American Railroads. Total carloads increased 3.4%, their strongest percentage gain in eight months, while carloads excluding coal climbed 4.5%. Fifteen of the 20 carload categories tracked by the AAR posted year-over-year increases in October, and 16 were higher through the first 10 months of 2026. The association said that breadth pointed to underlying industrial strength rather than simply a shift of freight from highways to rail. candidates.title: BLET members launch strike at Wheeling & Lake Erie
candidates.excerpt: BREWSTER, Ohio — Members of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen have launched a strike today against the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway. A BLET press release says the strike by 140 engineers and conductors began at noon. It was triggered, the union says, “by the railroad’s insistence on using managers to work as conductors. OCTA owns the former Santa Fe right-of-way along the Orange County coast used by Amtrak, Metrolink, and BNSF Railway trains. STB orders Union Pacific to make alleged rate hike threat video public
candidates.excerpt: The Surface Transportation Board has ordered Union Pacific to make public a recording of Chief Executive Jim Vena’s remarks to a shipper conference, rejecting the railroad’s appeal in a dispute over whether he threatened customers who oppose its proposed acquisition of Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC). The board’s Nov. 4 decision leaves in place a ruling requiring the recording to lose its confidential designation. The dispute has raised questions about transparency in the merger review, with the regulator expressing “serious concerns” about whether Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) had influenced stakeholder input on the proposed $85 billion transaction. The recording captures Vena’s address to the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers at its annual conference in Houston in March. Rival Canadian Pacific Kansas City sought its public release, arguing that Vena’s remarks allegedly threatening higher rates for shippers opposing the merger had chilled participation in the regulatory proceeding.
